notes: The three gates (requirements, then design, then tasks) all come before any code is written. Each one is short and says what is being approved: the requirements gate calls out its one change from the brief (merge keys now load instead of exiting 4) and names which choices to review, and the plan gate raises the temporary `set` refusal. Tasks 3.8 and 3.9 were added during implementation to fix bugs within requirements already approved, not to change requirements, so no gate was needed.
